item.title: Brownfield To Public Works Campus: New Milford advances Century Brass plan; riverside park could follow
item.description: New Milford plans to redevelop a former brass mill site into a municipal campus. This project includes a new fire-training tower assembled from shipping containers. The town acquired the contaminated property after a lengthy legal dispute. Moving public works will also free up land for a riverside park. This transformation reclaims industrial land for public use and green space.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 2018, an unbuilt penthouse shell under Hampshire House roof was marketed at $40 million
item.description: A half-finished penthouse situated on Manhattan's prestigious Billionaires' Row was auctioned for $6.765 million, a staggering 83% drop from its original $40 million price tag. The three-story residence within Hampshire House secured a contract following an intense online bidding war. The new owner is set to embark on a challenging and expensive task to bring the property to completion, wrapping up a lengthy real estate narrative.

item.title: Cooper’s Firehouse Home: Anchor restores 1906 patrol house; 9/11 legacy endures
item.description: In 2010, renowned journalist Anderson Cooper acquired a historic fire patrol house in Greenwich Village, prompting concerns among preservationists about the building's fate. Fortunately, it was preserved within the South Village Historic District. A poignant feature of the property is its connection to Keith Roma, a brave Fire Patrol member lost during the 9/11 tragedy. The residence now beautifully merges its rich history with a modern home.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Trump moves to scrap Biden-era carbon limits on US coal & gas power plants
item.description: The Trump administration plans to repeal Biden-era emission limits for power plants. This action removes restrictions on a major source of greenhouse gas pollution. The Environmental Protection Agency will announce the final rule soon. Environmental groups oppose the rollback, citing health and safety concerns. Legal challenges are expected against these policy changes.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: In 1990, Tennessee siblings planted 240 acres of former fields and pastures with loblolly pine...
item.description: In a significant conservation move, The Land Trust for Tennessee has permanently protected an expansive 852-acre estate. Siblings Mary Ann and John Sugg dedicated years to revitalizing farmland into lush forest. Their generous donation guarantees the landscape's preservation from future commercial development. Employing contemporary forestry techniques, the land trust oversees the property, ensuring a sustainable environmental legacy for generations to come.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: $8m campaign aims to return historic land to Wampanoag owners
item.description: A Native-led nonprofit launched an $8 million campaign to acquire a historic Martha's Vineyard property. This site holds deep ties to the Wampanoag community and its ancestral heritage. The Aquinnah Land Initiative aims to restore the former Aquinnah Shop restaurant for community use. A significant state grant supports the acquisition and long-term maintenance of the cliffside location.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: A 440-year-old Elizabethan mansion with 14 acres goes up for auction at £550,000–£600,000
item.description: A 440-year-old Grade I-listed Elizabethan mansion, Barlborough Hall, is heading to auction with a guide price of £550,000–£600,000. Dating to 1583, the historic property near Chesterfield boasts nearly 16,000 sq ft of accommodation and 14 acres of grounds. The mansion was linked to Sir Francis Rodes and architect Robert Smythson.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Meet Angus Liddell, Melbourne student who raised $10,000, launched a 10km charity swim
item.description: Recognized for his outstanding community service, Angus Liddell earned Kingston’s Young Citizen of the Year award. Through his initiative to host a charity swim event, he successfully generated substantial funds for various worthy causes. Additionally, he set a remarkable fundraising record at his college and engaged in lifesaving volunteer work, showcasing the meaningful influence that young leaders can have within their communities.

item.title: In 1997, a Western Australian coal mine closed; its 103-hectare void filled with 30bn litres and became Lake Kepwari
item.description: Lake Kepwari, a former coal mine void near Collie, Western Australia, has been transformed into a recreational hub. This artificial lake now offers swimming, boating, camping, and water sports for visitors. The transformation involved significant planning, water management, and infrastructure development over many years. Water was diverted from the Collie River South Branch to fill the large void. This project demonstrates repurposing industrial landscapes for tourism and community benefit.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Tennessee farmer leased 100 acres of century-old family land for solar instead of selling it; the 147 MW project is now powering homes and businesses
item.description: A Tennessee farmer chose to lease family land for a solar project. This decision allows continued ownership while generating income for future generations. The Yum Yum Solar facility, a 147-megawatt project, became operational in May 2026. This lease provides a steady income stream, addressing farming challenges and land fragmentation. The project highlights a growing trend of farmers balancing energy production with land preservation.
